NC-senate.statusNote: Primary held March 3, 2026 — Cooper (D) and Whatley (R) won their nominations.

candidates.name: Roy Cooper
candidates.background: Governor of North Carolina 2017–2025; NC Attorney General 2001–2017. Won the March 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate.

cost.label: Campaign platform: lower grocery costs, block anti-competitive mergers, ban algorithmic pricing (Ballotpedia)

health.label: Championed NC Medicaid expansion; platform: cap drug costs, protect ACA (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: Vetoed 2019 bill requiring sheriffs to cooperate with ICE (WBTV)

climate.label: Launched NC Clean Energy Plan as governor (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Record: teacher raises, pre-K expansion, Teaching Fellows; opposed voucher expansion (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Long-standing opposition to NC voter ID legislation (Ballotpedia)

candidates.name: Michael Whatley
candidates.background: Former Republican National Committee chairman and NC GOP chairman; earlier an energy-industry executive (Consumer Energy Alliance). Won the March 2026 Republican primary; endorsed by President Trump.

cost.label: Campaign: 'more money in your pockets,' fiscal responsibility, unleash American energy (campaign site)

immigration.label: '100% supportive' of securing the border and deportations (campaign site)

taxes.label: Campaign: fiscal responsibility, 'more money in your pockets' — no detailed tax plan published (campaign site)

climate.label: Campaign: energy independence, 'unleashing American energy' (campaign site)

safety.label: Campaign: 'back the blue without apology,' restore law and order, opposes cashless bail (campaign site)

repro.label: Campaign pledges 'protecting life' — no specifics published (campaign site)

democracy.label: Campaign: 'protect the ballot'; led election-integrity efforts as NC GOP chair (campaign site)
